title: Leap-second handling bug leads to transient double-counting of per-org quotas
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Summary: During a scheduled UTC leap-second insertion test in staging we observed a transient spike in per-org quota deductions for requests ingested around the leap-second boundary. The spike reproduces when the wall-clock includes a 23:59:60 timestamp and our per-window accumulator code maps timestamps to slot boundaries using naive UTC second arithmetic.

Impact: For a ~2 second window surrounding the leap-second event we saw duplicate increments for some keys (per-org and per-route) resulting in brief overcharging / quota exhaustions for affected orgs. Production did not experience a live leap-second at the time of discovery, but the logic is a correctness hole that will trigger on any deployment that encounters a 61-second minute (leap second) or similar non-monotonic clock adjustment (e.g., certain NTP corrections).

Repro steps (staging):
1) Deploy test harness that pushes 200 requests/sec for a single API key.
2) Use time-mock shim in edge shard to return a wall-clock sequence that includes 23:59:60 for a minute boundary.
3) Observe the per-org accumulator metrics and metering events emitted to the shard-aggregator. Duplicate meter events appear for ~0.8–1.5s window.

Why this is novel vs other rate/count bugs: Most recent metering bugs stem from shard/epoch overlap, duplicate ingestion, or policy-fanout. This issue is specifically a time-encoding edge-case: our slot-calculation converts timestamps -> epoch/slot using second-based floor math that assumes monotonic incrementing seconds. Leap seconds and some NTP-induced backwards jumps produce collisions where two different observed timestamps map into the same slot twice or a single logical second is mapped twice, leading to double-application of the same request in downstream aggregation path.

Immediate customer mitigation (already applied in staging):
- Disabled leap-second time-mock tests for public runs (so we don't trigger production alarms accidentally).
- Enabled an ingress-side dedupe guard: short lived request-id dedupe (1500ms) for high-volume keys at the edge. This prevents the most obvious duplicate counts while we work on a root fix.

Longer-term fix approach (choices under consideration):
A) Switch all window slot calculations to use a monotonic, leap-second–agnostic clock (preferred). Requires plumbing monotonic time through RPC traces and ensuring aggregator components that persist wall-clock for human reporting still receive a leap-aware timestamp.
B) Normalize timestamps at ingestion: convert any 23:59:60 to 23:59:59. This is a simpler patch but lossy for observability (human-readable logs will conceal the leap-second).
C) Add a robust dedupe layer in the shard-aggregator keyed by (org,key,route,unix-second,request-hash) for a short TTL; acts as a safety net but does not address root calibration and adds memory overhead.

We recommend A + short TTL dedupe as fallback during rollout.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for slot mapping logic with mocked leap-second and NTP-jump sequences.
- Integration test in staging that advances a monotonic clock and asserts per-org meter invariants across the boundary.
- Load test with 10k RPS harness injecting leap-second to validate dedupe safety net performance.
- Canary rollout to 2% of traffic after runtime-1.20 cut with a skewed time simulation to ensure zero regressions.

Telemetry & observability changes needed:
- New prometheus metric runtime.leapsecond.dedupe_events_total (counter) to track dedupe hits.
- Alert rule: if per-org meters show >3x normal variance in a 1m window and dedupe_events_total equals zero, page SRE.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests added and green.
- E2E staging harness shows 0 duplicate meters after monotonic-time patch.
- Canary shows <1ms p99 added latency, and dedupe fallback rate <0.1% of requests.
- Docs updated (console and rollout) describing the change in epoch semantics for auditors.

mitigation: Ingress short-ttl dedupe (1500ms) enabled for high-throughput keys; SRE notified to temporarily relax per-org alerting on quota spikes tied to leap-second window. This is a temporary stopgap, will be removed once monotonic fix is live and canary passes.
root_cause_summary: Slot calculation used wall-clock seconds and naive floor division into fixed-size windows. When an extra second (23:59:60) appears, timing mapping produced overlapping slots and the same request got ingested and aggregated twice due to idempotency assumptions downstream being violated by the unexpected timestamp semantics.

monitoring_queries: Elasticsearch: shard-aggregator logs where timestamp=="23:59:60" and event_type=="meter_emit"
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: leap seconds are rare, but the correctness hole interacts with multiple prior race mitigations we've deployed (dedupe and shard backfills). Fixing now avoids potential customer billing anomalies if we ever run in an environment that applies leap-second semantics (some clouds and time services do).
